Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-21 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions Eng); Jenna (CTO, QuantNode), Mark (Platform), Sofia (ML infra), Tom (SRE)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros — I'm Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya is our systems SE, Diego handles solutions and the benchmarks.
[00:10] Jenna: Hi all, Jenna here. We're excited — we want to understand whether Redwood Hosted is good enough or if we need Dedicated or Private for our tokenflow use case.
[00:17] Mark: Yep, a lot of it is p95 and burst behavior, also streaming start latency because we do progressive summarization for live calls.
[00:25] Priya: Great context — can you run me through current stack and traffic patterns? rough numbers are fine.
[00:33] Sofia: Sure. We have a microservice that ingests live transcripts and makes a streaming summarize call plus a final full-summary call. Steady state is ~60 qps, average response 120 tokens. Peak bursts hit 450 qps for 60-90s during scheduled events. We aim for p95 start-of-stream < 300ms and p95 full response < 1.2s for 120-token responses.
[01:02] Diego: Helpful. Are you currently doing batching or prefix caching? how's your KV cache used?
[01:10] Mark: We have rudimentary local cache for repeated prefixes, but nothing global. No KV caching at model layer yet.
[01:15] Priya: ok. On Redwood we typically use a combination: prefix/KV caching plus low-latency streaming paths. For hosted, small bursts are absorbed by autoscale but deep bursts depend on quota and capacity — Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools so you get predictability. Private gives you full control but requires infra setup.
[01:36] Jenna: Cost is a concern — ideally we want to avoid overpaying for idle GPUs but can't have p95 regressions.
[01:42] Alex: Totally. Part of the benchmark we'll show is tokens/sec under continuous and bursty conditions and the p95 delta with prefix caching on vs off.
[01:50] Tom: For our ops team, a big question is network: VPC peering and private endpoints. Can Redwood Private integrate with our KMS/HSM for key management?
[01:59] Priya: Yes — Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations, and we can run in your VPC with a private control plane. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our keys or bring-your-own KMS for dedicated contracts.
[02:15] Sofia: Security docs? We need SOC2 report and pen test artifacts.
[02:19] Alex: We'll share SOC2 Type II and our security pack. I'll drop links after the call.
[02:25] Jenna: Great. Now on performance, can you talk about p95 behavior across model sizes and quantization? we plan to evaluate 7B-13B compressed models.
[02:33] Priya: Sure. Roughly: smaller models (7B quantized) give lower latency per token and better concurrency, but quality with your prompt set matters. Quantization reduces memory and increases throughput but can increase CPU/GPU kernel overhead in some sequences. For streaming start latency, the runtime optimizes the first token path; we typically see start latency improvements when continuous batching is disabled for streamer sessions.
[02:55] Diego: We should define benchmark scenarios. I'd suggest: 1) steady-state 60 qps continuous generation (120 tokens avg) 2) scheduled burst 450 qps for 90s 3) short streaming start latency test — concurrent 200 streams sending initial tokens. We'll measure p95 start and p95 full completion and tokens/sec overall.
[03:15] Mark: Sounds good. How many tokens/sec can Redwood tokenize and serve per GPU for our 13B quantized model?
[03:23] Priya: ballpark: with 13B-quant on an A100-ish equivalent in Dedicated, you might see 8k-12k tokens/sec steady-state per GPU depending on batch policies. With prefix caching, effective user-perceived throughput can be much higher for repeated prompts. Hosted shared pools may show variance — that's why we run the sandbox.
[03:44] Jenna: If we go Hosted, what's the expected p95 variability during a burst? we need an SLO for user experience.
[03:52] Diego: For shared-hosted, p95 can stretch by 20-40% during noisy neighbor bursts if autoscale lag happens. With Dedicated you get tighter p95 bounds — usually within 5-10% of baseline under autoscale policy tuned for your burst profile.
[04:07] Tom: Any suggestions for smoothing bursts without huge cost?
[04:11] Priya: yes: 1) pre-warm Dedicated capacity for scheduled events, 2) use short-lived cache warmers, 3) tiered routing — route non-critical calls to cheaper quantized variants, critical ones to high-priority pool. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization settings per workload.
[04:30] Jenna: Route to cheaper variant — how much p95 delta are we talking between 13B and 7B?
[04:36] Priya: Typical p95 improvement with 7B is ~30-50% faster for short completions but you might lose some output quality. We can run A/B with your prompts to quantify quality/latency tradeoffs.
[04:47] Mark: For streaming open token per second, do we pay per token the same across Hosted/Dedicated?
[04:52] Alex: Pricing varies: Hosted is usage-based per-token. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model — you pay for reserved GPUs and then tokens are metered differently, often cheaper per-token for heavy users. We'll include a rough cost model in the worksheet.
[05:05] Sofia: Good. On the benchmark — what artifacts do you need from our side?
[05:09] Priya: A small prompt set (3-5 canonical prompts), a transcript sample for streaming, and your expected SLOs. Also, indicate preferred model family (we'll test 7B and 13B quantized variants) and whether to enable prefix caching.
[05:22] Jenna: We'll provide those by Friday.
[05:25] Diego: For the benchmark run, we'll provision a hosted sandbox with isolated pool and run three tests: steady-state, scheduled burst, and streaming start. We'll produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec and error rates. Link will be shared.
[05:40] Mark: Nice. We also care about cold-starts for rare models when you do a canary rollout — what's cold-start p95?
[05:46] Priya: Cold-start depends on model size and whether kernels are jittered into memory; for quantized 13B on cold node might be several seconds to tens of seconds. Redwood mitigates with warmers and canary pre-warming during rollout. For Dedicated, you control how many warmed replicas exist.
[06:05] Jenna: Any gotchas with KV cache and streaming interactions? we've seen cache misses blow up latency.
[06:11] Priya: Yep — cache invalidation and miss storms are tricky. We recommend token-level eviction policies and gradual cache population. Redwood Console shows cache hit rates so you can tune TTLs.
[06:23] Tom: Ok, ops question: logs and audit trails — will we get per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdown?
[06:28] Diego: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms and tracing hooks you can wire to your tracing system. For Private, logs can be pushed to your syslog/S3.
[06:40] Jenna: Any regulatory note about data residency? we have EU customers.
[06:44] Alex: Hosted has region controls; for strict residency you can use Private in-region or Dedicated region pinned. We'll highlight options in the follow-up doc.
[06:55] Sofia: Regarding the benchmark results: will you include variance across runs and guidance on expected p95 with caching on/off?
[07:01] Priya: yes, we'll show baseline with no cache, then warm cache run, and a mixed traffic run. We'll highlight expected p95 improvements attributable to each optimization.
[07:12] Jenna: Great. A few closing logistical items: who owns follow-up?
[07:16] Alex: I'll coordinate and send the security pack and pricing worksheet. Priya will run the benchmark. Diego will help interpret results and do the Dedicated sizing. Jenna will share prompts.
[07:26] Jenna: OK, thanks. Any immediate concerns?
[07:29] Tom: latency budgets for network hops — let's include a short note in the benchmark about measured egress times from our VPC to Redwood edge.
[07:36] Priya: We'll add a network measurement step.
[07:39] Alex: Perfect. I'll schedule follow-up for early week of 2027-07-26 and send the links. Thanks everyone.
